newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA says outpatient revenue grows.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA says outpatient revenue grows.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp said outpatient revenues increased to 38 percent of total patient revenues in the first quarter from 36 percent in the same quarter of 1996.
The shift in revenue mix was caused by growth in homecare services, outpatient surgery and other ancillary services, said the largest U.S. hospital company.
Columbia said Wednesday that revenues totaled $5.3 billion for the quarter ended March 31, up eight percent from $5 billion in the year-ago quarter.
Shares in Columbia were up 3/4 to 35-1/8.

Same-facility net revenues grew eight percent on the quarter, based on same-facility adjusted admissions growth of five percent and same-facility inpatient admissions growth of two percent. Surgery cases at company hospitals and ambulatory surgery centers increased five percent on a same-facility basis. Improvements in same-facility patient volumes are understated as a result of this year's first quarter having one fewer day due to leap year in 1996, Columbia said.
Columbia said it reduced its total debt by about $342 million in the quarter, improving its ratio of debt to capitalization to 40.1 percent at March 31, from 47.5 percent at March 31, 1996.
